017package org.apache.juneau.commons.concurrent;
018
019import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.AssertionUtils.*;
020
021import java.util.concurrent.*;
022import java.util.concurrent.atomic.*;
023
024/**
025 * Built-in default {@link ReplayCache}: a per-process, {@link ConcurrentHashMap}-backed seen-identifier set with
026 * self-eviction bounded by each record's own {@code expiresAtMs}.
027 *
028 * <p>
029 * <b>Not shareable across process instances by design.</b> Two separate JVMs (or two instances behind a load
030 * balancer) each holding their own {@link InMemoryReplayCache} will not see each other's recorded identifiers, so
031 * an identifier consumed against one instance and then submitted again against the other is <b>not</b> caught.
032 * Consumers who need cross-node single-use enforcement must supply a {@link ReplayCache} backed by a store shared
033 * across every node instead of relying on this default.
034 *
035 * <p>
036 * <b>Memory bound (size honestly).</b> An identifier is retained only until its own {@code expiresAtMs}, so the
037 * map's steady-state size is bounded by the product of the <i>distinct-identifier submission rate</i> and the
038 * identifier lifetime &mdash; i.e. roughly the number of distinct, still-unexpired identifiers outstanding at
039 * once, plus at most one lifetime's worth of already-expired records awaiting the next sweep.  Under a high rate
040 * with a long lifetime this is not inherently small; consumers should size accordingly, or supply a store-backed
041 * {@link ReplayCache} with server-side expiry.  There is deliberately <b>no</b> hard cap that drops
042 * still-unexpired identifiers: doing so would silently weaken replay detection by letting an evicted-but-valid
043 * identifier be submitted again.
044 *
045 * <p>
046 * <b>Eviction is throttled.</b> Sweeping out already-expired records is an O(n) scan, so it runs at most once per
047 * {@link #DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS} rather than on every call (which would make {@link #checkAndRecord}
048 * effectively O(n) per invocation under load).  The sweep exists purely to bound memory.
049 *
050 * <p>
051 * <b>Thread-safety.</b> {@link #checkAndRecord(String, long)} is safe for concurrent invocation: the
052 * check-and-record step is a single {@link ConcurrentHashMap#putIfAbsent} call, so of any two concurrent calls
053 * with the same identifier, exactly one observes a first-seen (<jk>true</jk>) outcome.  The throttled sweep is
054 * guarded by an atomic compare-and-set so at most one thread sweeps per interval.
055 *
056 * @since 10.0.0
057 */
058public class InMemoryReplayCache implements ReplayCache {
059
060   /** Default minimum interval, in milliseconds, between opportunistic expired-record sweeps. */
061   public static final long DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 1000L;
062
063   private final ConcurrentHashMap<String,Long> seen = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
064   private final long sweepIntervalMs;
065   private final AtomicLong nextSweepAtMs = new AtomicLong();
066
067   /**
068    * Constructor using the {@link #DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS default} sweep interval.
069    */
070   public InMemoryReplayCache() {
071      this(DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS);
072   }
073
074   /**
075    * Constructor.
076    *
077    * @param sweepIntervalMs The minimum interval, in milliseconds, between opportunistic expired-record sweeps.
078    *    {@code 0} sweeps on every call (useful in tests that assert eviction behavior). Must be {@code >= 0}.
079    */
080   InMemoryReplayCache(long sweepIntervalMs) {
081      if (sweepIntervalMs < 0)
082         throw new IllegalArgumentException("sweepIntervalMs " + sweepIntervalMs + " must be >= 0");
083      this.sweepIntervalMs = sweepIntervalMs;
084   }
085
086   @Override /* ReplayCache */
087   public boolean checkAndRecord(String id, long expiresAtMs) {
088      assertArgNotNull("id", id);
089      maybeEvictExpired();
090      return seen.putIfAbsent(id, expiresAtMs) == null;
091   }
092
093   /**
094    * Sweeps expired records at most once per {@link #sweepIntervalMs}. The atomic compare-and-set on
095    * {@code nextSweepAtMs} both throttles the sweep and ensures a single sweeper per window; a losing thread
096    * simply skips the sweep (its own {@code putIfAbsent} still runs, so no identifier is ever missed).
097    */
098   private void maybeEvictExpired() {
099      var now = System.currentTimeMillis();
100      var next = nextSweepAtMs.get();
101      if (now < next)
102         return;
103      if (! nextSweepAtMs.compareAndSet(next, now + sweepIntervalMs))
104         return;
105      seen.values().removeIf(expiresAt -> expiresAt <= now);
106   }
107}
